plan.title: An off day: one light rest-day text, no push

context.text: Plan's yours, Jordan. I'll hold you to it. You in?
Enjoy the weekend. Rest day tomorrow, back at it Tuesday 🏃

transcript.text: Morning, Jordan! Today's a rest day, so let those legs recover. Tomorrow we're back at it: 30 minutes at the park at 6 pm 🏃
Good, that's what rest days are for. Tomorrow's 30 minutes at the park at 6 pm, and I'll be looking for that Strava screenshot afterward. Ready for it?

checks.reason: Opens with "Morning, Jordan!", a warm greeting with their name.
Says it's a rest day with no push, just "let those legs recover."
No guilt or urgency in the text.
Two short sentences with no question, within the limit.
Plain text with one emoji as punctuation, no markdown.
Warm, energetic and not overfamiliar, with one emoji at the end.
Adds a push for tomorrow's run and asks "Ready for it?" on a rest day, not light.
No guilt or fake urgency, just reassurance on rest days.
Runs to four sentences and restates the time, place and proof for tomorrow.
Plain words with no markdown or filler.
Warm and sincere in tone, without overfamiliarity or emoji rows.

conversation.reason: ZOH 2 replies to "legs needed it" by restating tomorrow's run and asking "Ready for it?", a lock-in and follow-up the rest day shouldn't carry.

grade.summary: ZOH's opening rest-day text was short, warm and used Jordan's name, as expected. The reply to "legs needed it" broke the rest-day rule by pushing tomorrow's run, restating the time and proof, and asking for a yes, so the regression case fails.
